screen: Production Brand kit, approved kit (phone 390, full page), Stage 5 pass 2

expected_differences: Demo Coffee Co. replaces the Lab’s creator fixture, with business navigation and the Business tab correctly selected.
The saved brand’s #0B0D0E, #C8FF3D and #F7F7F5 swatches and Archivo/Inter typography direction are customer content, not changes to TapMart’s interface tokens.
The profile photograph appears as an honest fallback, explicitly labelled “Logo from your profile, not yet part of the kit”; no approved logo is fabricated.
This is an already-approved kit, so “Current brand · Approved” and “Suggest improvements” are appropriate. A pending proposal and its Approve control need not appear in this state.
Creator earnings, vehicles and the large graphite identity region are absent because this is a management screen, not the Profile shown in the supplied Lab reference.
keep: Mineral canvas, ink text, muted supporting copy and restrained dividers without floating cards or shadows.
The 16px phone gutters, strong page title and orderly sequence of logo, colours, typography, photo style, voice, content style and rules.
The full-width, approximately 48px-high Suggest improvements control with an ink label, visible border and 8px corners.
Photo references displayed at distinct source ratios with restrained 4px corners rather than uniform cropped tiles.
Literal Approved status, explicit logo provenance and the statement that changes require the user’s decision.
Settings back navigation, account switching, search, messages, notifications and the selected Business navigation edge.
review.readiness_note: Sign off visually at 390px. The supplied Lab is a Profile reference, so this is a system-level transfer assessment rather than a same-screen comparison. The capture preserves the visible saved-kit data and management controls; proposal generation, approval gating and persistence still require runtime verification.
review.why: The production screen carries the approved mineral-neutral surface treatment, Archivo-style heading hierarchy, operational supporting text and flat structural layout into a quieter utility context. Content fits the 358px working width without clipped swatches, crowded controls or navigation overlap. The two photo references retain different proportions, while the profile-image fallback is contained and explained. Cobalt remains concentrated in navigation and meaningful controls; the lime swatch belongs to the saved brand. There is no monetary content to merge or misrepresent. This reading state has no source-to-commitment assembly requiring a 12px joint, so omitting a decorative offset is correct. No visible implementation drift warrants a change.
review.verdict: Yes—Frame Shift is faithfully transferred to this approved Brand kit at 390px, with its real data, literal state and visible management functionality preserved.
